conclusion: Positive CPU integration feasibility for the explicit audited decision-schema subset on existing A28 runtime; no arbitrary JSON Schema enforcement or GPU latency/readiness claim.
limits: Current installed strict converter accepts examples violating not,uniqueItems,unknownformat,and pattern+maxLength; explicit policy rejection is essential.
Grammar enforces audited structure but cannot prove visual facts, correct temporal support, uniqueness of fact IDs under the original schema, or legal conclusions.
A valid partial prefix truncated by token/time limits still fails complete JSON/schema validation; no repair or unconstrained fallback.
HF adapter calls .item() on the last token and moves a CPU bitmask to scores device every token; actual CUDA synchronization/copy/masking overhead and endpoint latency remain unmeasured.
Schemas with different frame alias count/fact sets may miss the bounded cache and incur cold compilation; startup warmup proves the normal16-frame schema only.
Constrained generation changes token selection; quality and recall must be compared with the frozen pipeline, and no speed-only sampling changes are justified.
Canonical prefixItems exact-once feasibility is separately proven; current policy rejects it. Adoption requires explicit trusted transform/version binding and new source/runtime proofs.
